evidence_items.summary: The protection of the natural environment during armed conflict has become an increasingly significant concern in international humanitarian law (IHL), given the devastating environmental consequences of contemporary warfare. Armed conflicts frequently result in the destruction of forests, contamination of water resources, degradation of agricultural land, pollution of the atmosphere, and damage to ecosystems essential for human survival. These consequences threaten civilian populations, undermine public health, compromise food security, and impede post-conflict recovery. Although existing international humanitarian law instruments, particularly the Additional Protocols I and II of 1977 to the Geneva Conventions of 1949, provide specific protections against certain forms of environmental damage, significant challenges remain concerning the interpretation, implementation, and enforcement of the applicable legal standards. This paper examines the legal framework governing the protection of the natural environment during armed conflict, with particular emphasis on the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) Guidelines on the Protection of the Natural Environment in Armed Conflict and the subsequent implementation guidance developed to facilitate their practical application. It evaluates the principles of distinction, proportionality, precaution, military necessity, and the prohibition of widespread, long-term and severe environmental damage, while highlighting the relationship between environmental protection and the protection of civilians and civilian objects. The paper further examines the institutional, operational, and normative challenges that impede the effective implementation of environmental protection obligations by states, armed forces, and other relevant actors.
evidence_items.title: Protection of The Natural Environment (PNE) During Armed Conflict and The Implementation Guidance On PNE

evidence_items.summary: The palm stem borer, Oryctes elegans . Pell, is considered one of the most destructive pests attacking date palm trunks in the middle Euphrates region. In Babylon governorate, many old orchards suffer from severe infestation, which often leads farmers to cut the trees. During 2024-2025, we conducted both laboratory and field trials at Al-Mussaib Technical College and in three private orchards in Babylon. In the laboratory, 90 last instar larvae were tested (10 larvae for each replicate, three replicates per insecticide). In the field, we used 72 palm trees distributed in three orchards following Randomized Complete Block Design. Each orchard contained 24 palms: 9 for trunk injection, 9 for conventional spraying, and 6 as untreated control. For injection, we drilled a hole of about 0.5 cm diameter and 12 cm depth at a 45-degree angle, at 1.5 m height, injected 1 liter solution per palm and closed the hole with wax. Three insecticides were evaluated: Carbaryl (20 g/L), Fipronil (2 ml/L), and Chlorpyrifos 48% (3 ml/L). After 24 hours in lab, mortality was 79.0% for Carbaryl, 74.26% for Fipronil, and 63.26% for Chlorpyrifos. Statistical analysis showed significant differences (F = 14.51, p = 0.0050, LSD0.05 = 7.33). After five days, mortality increased to 85.66%, 78.43%, and 72.63% respectively (F = 8.60, p = 0.0172, LSD0.05 = 7.70). Under field conditions, light trap catches decreased from 13 to 0 insects/trap for Carbaryl (100% reduction) and from 15 to 0 for Fipronil (100%), while Chlorpyrifos decreased from 14 to 2 (85.7%). These results indicate that trunk injection, particularly with Carbaryl, can achieve complete control after three months and could be recommended for Babylon orchards.
evidence_items.title: Field and Laboratory Evaluation of Trunk Injection with Three Insecticides for Controlling the Palm Stem Borer Oryctes elegans Prell in Babylon Province, Iraq

evidence_items.summary: This study examines the role of supervision in optimizing the performance of Heads of Work Units (Kasatker) at the Bekasi District Police, focusing on supervision mechanisms, supporting and inhibiting factors, and strategies for improvement. Using a descriptive qualitative approach, data were collected through literature reviews, non-participatory observation, and analysis of official documents and regulations, with validity ensured through source triangulation. The findings identify three complementary supervision mechanisms: inherent, functional, and professional/ethical supervision, which contribute to operational effectiveness, budget accountability, and leadership integrity. Supervision effectiveness is supported by measurable performance indicators, periodic evaluations, and technological integration. However, challenges include limited resources, organizational culture, excessive supervisory pressure, and the complexity of densely populated jurisdictions. The study concludes that optimizing Kasatker performance requires integrated supervision mechanisms, consistent implementation, technological innovation, and strategies adapted to regional characteristics. Future research should incorporate primary field data to provide deeper insights into supervision effectiveness and organizational performance.
evidence_items.title: The Role of Supervision in Optimizing the Performance of Work Unit Heads at the Bekasi District Police

The analysis identified 20,795 apple-centered gene correspondences and prioritized 269 expression-supported candidates, 190 locally collinear candidates, 24 candidates supported by external apple leaf transcriptomes, and five candidates supported in both external leaf contexts. The dataset also contains frozen pathway mappings, supplementary numerical tables, and reproducibility documentation. evidence_items.summary: Radar-based human activity recognition (HAR) offers privacy and robustness over camera-based methods, yet remains computationally demanding for edge deployment. We present the first application of spiking neural networks (SNNs) for radar-based HAR on aircraft marshaling signal classification. Our novel hybrid architecture combines a pre-trained convolutional backbone for spatial feature extraction and leaky integrate-and-fire neurons for temporal processing, inherently capturing gesture dynamics. The model reduces trainable parameters by 88% with under 1% accuracy loss compared to existing state of the art methods, and generalizes well to the Soli gesture dataset. Through systematic comparisons with other three artificial neural network architectures, we demonstrate the trade-offs of spiking computation in terms of accuracy, latency, memory, and energy, establishing SNNs as an efficient and competitive solution for radar-based HAR.
evidence_items.title: Spatiotemporal Radar Gesture Recognition with Hybrid Spiking Neural Networks: Balancing Accuracy and Efficiency

evidence_items.summary: Summary Biofilms are major barrier to effective antimicrobial therapy, with Staphylococcus aureus biofilms posing a particularly persistent clinical challenge. Natural products are a major reservoir for novel antimicrobials, as they are a valuable source of structurally diverse bioactive molecules with fungi representing a rich but untapped source of such metabolites. This thesis investigates the secondary metabolism of Samsoniella aurantia, Neonothopanus nambi, and three Laburnicola nematophila strains. Following cultivation under liquid and solid fermentation conditions, fungal extracts were profiled by HPLC-DAD/MS, and separated by preparative HPLC. Subsequently, pure compounds were structurally characterized using 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy and HR-ESI-MS. The isolated compounds were screened for antimicrobial activity against fungi and Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as for cytotoxicity against various cell lines. In total, eight compounds comprising 2-pyridones, tetramic acids and sesquiterpenoid derivatives, were selected following initial screening for detailed evaluation against S. aureus biofilms. Robust and biologically relevant in vitro assays were used to evaluate the effects of compounds on bacterial growth, biofilm formation and reduction, surface attachment, metabolic activity, membrane integrity, cell viability, and biofilm architecture. Endpoint measurements were complemented by kinetic assays to assess the onset and progression of treatment effects, as well as potential recovery following treatment. A continuous flow cell biofilm model was further established and optimized to enable reproducible S. aureus attachment and compound evaluation under more physiologically relevant conditions. Time-lapse confocal laser scanning microscopy was applied in both microtiter plate- and flow-cell-based experiments to visualize spatial organization, cell viability and structural changes in real time.
evidence_items.title: Exploring fungal secondary metabolites to target Staphylococcus aureus biofilms

evidence_items.summary: Research institutions increasingly need to know what software they produce and use, who maintains it, and how it contributes to impact and evaluation. Open Source Program Offices (OSPOs) need evidence to show the value of their open source policies, and funders and infrastructures need visibility into software assets and their sustainability. Research software is also fragile: it is spread across many forges, registries, and platforms, and it is exposed to "software collapse" as its dependencies change. This presentation introduces OSPO-Radar, a two-year project (June 2025 – June 2027) led by Software Heritage and funded by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. OSPO-Radar is the missing layer between institutions and the Software Heritage universal source code archive. It lets organizations build and curate their own software collection in four steps. First, they define their scope as a list of URLs. OSPO-Radar then collects metadata from forges and registries and preserves the source code in Software Heritage with persistent identifiers (SWHIDs). Finally, institutions manage the collection through a dashboard and a public API. A companion Insights report helps institutions find their software by deriving repository URLs from their email domains in commit history. The talk covers: the needs of academic OSPO managers the platform's benefits for visibility, governance, recognition and preservation the first MVP, deployed in September 2026, with a live demo the roadmap toward a production-ready release It closes with ways to take part, as a co-design partner, pilot institution, member advisor, or open source contributor. Mutualisation of shared infrastructure is key to sustainability.
evidence_items.title: Building a window into the Software Heritage Cathedral: OSPO-Radar Deep Dive

evidence_items.summary: The development of multifunctional surfaces on titanium implants is a critical strategy for mitigating post-operative infections and enhancing long-term clinical integration. This study investigates a dual-stage surface modification of the Ti6Al4V alloy, combining shifted Laser Surface Texturing (sLST) with functional ethanol-based silver coatings. The novelty of this research lies in the synergistic combination of advanced sLST surface engineering, which creates a hexagonal "reservoir" topography, and the stable functionalization of these complex structures with antimicrobial silver particles. Initially, the substrates were laser-processed to create a defined hexagonal surface morphology, followed by the deposition of silver-containing) and silver-free coatings via dip-coating and subsequent heat treatment. Comprehensive surface characterization confirmed a homogeneous distribution of silver particles within the porous laser-textured structure, with silver concentrations in the resulting extracts reaching several mg/l. Biological evaluation revealed that the silver-doped coatings achieved nearly 100% antibacterial efficacy against Escherichia coli after 24 h, showing zero or only negligible colony growth compared to the silver-free and reference samples. Cytotoxicity testing with extracts using L929 fibroblasts demonstrated that all modified surfaces maintained relative metabolic activity above 70% threshold, thus qualifying as non-toxic according to ISO 10993-5 standards. Despite this high metabolic viability, microscopic analysis revealed localized impairments in cell morphology, suggesting a complex cellular response that may be influenced by preparation-related factors. The integration of sLST texturing with Ag-doped ethanol coatings represents a highly effective approach for producing antimicrobial titanium surfaces with maintained cytocompatibility, offering significant potential for advanced orthopaedic and dental applications.
evidence_items.title: Bioactive and antibacterial Ti-6Al-4V surfaces prepared by shifted laser texturing and silver thin film deposition

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The "Provisional specification.pdf" introduces a comprehensive security architecture for governing autonomous artificial intelligence agents across isolated runtimes, administrative domains, and hardware environments . As AI agents increasingly invoke external tools and modify persistent data, the system distinguishes between an agent's ability to compute and its authority to execute consequential external effects . The architecture intercepts proposed agent operations, holding them in a non-effective state while a protected enforcement domain evaluates operation-specific authorization conditions and commits validation evidence . A scoped, non-bearer finality capability is then verified at an effectuation sink before the operation can produce real-world consequences . The specification covers advanced technical mechanisms including micro-virtual-machine isolation, task-preserving context minimization, distributed revocation, and hardware-level command accounting . Why You Should Download This Document You should download this specification if you are building, securing, or deploying autonomous AI agents that interact with enterprise resources, financial systems, or cloud infrastructure. It provides a detailed blueprint for preventing unauthorized external actions caused by prompt injection, compromised models, or hallucinated tool invocations. The document offers actionable implementations for deploying agents within virtual machines, micro-virtual machines, and OS-level containers while maintaining strict cryptographic and hardware-assisted oversight over API requests, network egress, and persistent memory mutations .
evidence_items.title: The Ultimate Guide to AI Agent Security and Sandboxing

evidence_items.summary: Slide deck of a public talk titled ' Free as in extraction: AI and the digital commons ' delivered online by Rohini Lakshané for the  Future of the Commons on 22 October 2026. Description of the talk : AI’s appetite for data is turning collective intellectual labour into private power. From Wikipedia and public archives to journalism and community histories, collectively produced knowledge feeds proprietary systems. Rohini Lakshané examines what this transformation means for the digital commons: the knowledge, infrastructure, and human labour that sustain a collaborative online world. Connecting the geopolitics of knowledge with feminist critiques of AI, she traces how automated systems erase authorship and political context, privilege dominant languages and perspectives, and devalue the work of volunteers and professionals. For marginalised communities, inclusion in training data can coexist with exclusion from decisions. Drawing on her work on online harms, particularly technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), she examines how AI increasingly enables and amplifies abuse through non-consensual synthetic imagery, impersonation, and gendered disinformation. She connects these harms to the silencing of women and marginalised communities, showing how safety, consent, and accountability shape who can participate in the commons. Moving beyond copyright disputes, the talk explores community consent, collective stewardship, benefit-sharing, and public investment in open infrastructure, arguing for a future in which the people sustaining the commons participate in its governance.
evidence_items.title: Free as in extraction: AI and the digital commons

evidence_items.summary: Unrefereed AI-assisted research candidate. A dispatcher sends each arriving job to one of two identical first-come first-served servers, knowing the job's size and both workloads. Xie, Hyytiä and Righter (ACM SIGMETRICS Performance Evaluation Review 53(4) (2026) 42–48; arXiv:2509.21693v1) studied a fluid version of this problem and conjectured that, with two servers, the relative workload imbalance increases along every optimal path. This package solves their two-server problem exactly. For every mean-one job-size law that is not a point mass, and every load below one, a single quadrature of D(h) = E|S − h| gives the optimal value, the optimal feedback policy and the optimal path from every state. In words: jobs smaller than a cutoff go to the shorter queue and larger jobs to the longer one; the cutoff depends only on the relative imbalance and rises as the queues drift apart; once one queue is empty it is kept exactly busy (at loads of at least 1/2). The verification allows idling, reflection, atoms and unbounded support. It proves the conjecture as posed (sizes with a density), extends it to all nondegenerate laws, and shows that the optimal workload path is unique; for deterministic sizes the conjecture fails. The heavy-traffic limit (1 − ρ)V → P(S ≥ m)x 2 , with m the work median (atoms at m split), corrects a factor in the source's Proposition 3 and matches the heavy-traffic constant of the CARD policy of Xie, Grosof and Scully; the fluid limit is proved and the link to the stochastic queue is heuristic (and, like the CARD result, assumes finite variance). Further proved results: an exact rational controller for finite size laws, certified bounds with an implementable bin policy, Wasserstein stability, an exact enclosure for an infinite-variance Pareto law, and the cost of noisy size estimates. In the running example (sizes 1/2 and 3/2, load 3/4) the optimal cost is 33/28 against 3/2 for balanced routing.
evidence_items.title: Exact optimal dispatching to two fluid queues: closed form, heavy traffic and stochastic evidence

evidence_items.summary: This study examined the relationship between the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and electricity metering in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. The study was motivated by persistent challenges in the electricity sector, including inadequate metering, estimated billing, billing disputes, limited consumer awareness, and concerns regarding the effectiveness of regulatory enforcement. The study adopted a survey research design. The population of the study was 1,057,858 active electricity consumers in Akwa Ibom State, while a sample size of 400 respondents was determined using the Taro Yamane formula. Six Local Government Areas Uyo, Itu, Eket, Oron, Ikot Ekpene and Abak were purposively selected to provide geographical representation. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed using frequency, percentage, mean, linear regression and Pearson Product Moment Correlation, with statistical decisions based on a 0.05 level of significance. A total of 400 questionnaires were administered, of which 356 were properly completed and returned, representing an 89% response rate. The findings indicated a relatively high level of public awareness of NERC, as 78.4% of respondents reported awareness of the Commission. However, awareness of electricity consumer rights and familiarity with NERC's customer protection regulations were comparatively low. The findings further showed that respondents perceived NERC's financial regulation as contributing to billing transparency, with a mean score of 3.75, while perceptions concerning the reduction of estimated billing and protection against estimated billing were below the 3.00 decision benchmark. The study concludes that although NERC has established regulatory mechanisms intended to improve electricity metering, billing transparency and consumer protection, gaps remain in effective implementation, consumer awareness and protection from estimated billing.
evidence_items.title: THE NIGERIAN ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION (NERC) AND ELECTRICITY METERING IN AKWA IBOM STATE

evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT   Global optimization is an important branch of computational mathematics that finds the applications in every walk of life. The real-world science and engineering optimization applications are becoming more and more complex in nature and are generally multimodal. The conventional optimization methods fail to optimize such complex multimodal problems. Hence there is always an increasing demand for efficient and robust optimization strategies. In recent years, algorithms based on random process have become popular and are an alternative to conventional methods in optimization. The Stochastic Algorithms are based on random process and most of them are the extraction of natural phenomenon for problem solving. The objective of this paper is to investigate and analyze stochastic algorithms on complex multimodal optimization problems. The comprehensive analysis of different stochastic algorithms is carried out on a set of standard benchmark problems with 10, 30 and 50 dimensions. The algorithmic suitability, robustness and convergence rate of each will be investigated. evidence_items.summary: The claim that cultural events build a country's international image is widely asserted and rarely measured against the alternative explanations that could produce the same correlation. This article assembles a fourteen-region panel for Uzbekistan and a thirteen-country benchmark panel, and separates the event to image relationship into three measurable constructs: the concentration of the event portfolio, the efficiency with which event activity is converted first into international attention and then into visitor revenue, and corridor embeddedness, a construct introduced here to capture whether a region's calendar sits inside an established route and season. Event activity is distributed almost twice as evenly across regions as the attention it produces, with a Gini coefficient of 0.337 against 0.611. Event days convert into international mentions at an elasticity of 1.72 to 2.06 that survives every control, so events do generate attention. The transmission from attention to arrivals is bounded by accommodation capacity rather than by attention itself: the mentions elasticity falls from 0.831 to 0.421 once rooms enter, while the rooms elasticity of 0.588 carries a t statistic of 14.81. The cross-national ladder then removes the headline result entirely. The elasticity of tourism receipts with respect to signature events falls monotonically from 2.066 to 0.928 to 0.942 to minus 0.257 as arrivals, population and regional bloc are held constant, and it loses significance at the second step. RU Утверждение о том, что культурные мероприятия формируют международный имидж страны, широко распространено, однако его редко оценивают количественно с учётом альтернативных факторов, способных обусловить аналогичную взаимосвязь. В данной статье сформирована панель данных по 14 регионам Узбекистана и сравнительная панель по 13 странам.

evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in video generation have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, placing greater demands on reliable AI-generated video detection. Existing artifact-based detectors typically identify generation artifacts as evidence for source prediction, yet they may either fail to recognize subtle artifacts or reach the correct source decision without faithfully identifying the evidence underlying it. In this work, we systematically investigate how to design and train effective artifact detectors and formulate artifact detection as a structured process comprising three complementary capabilities: Inspection Planning, which determines what should be examined; Evidence Verification, which verifies whether the inspected content exhibits genuine generation artifacts; and Evidence Aggregation, which integrates the verified evidence into the final source decision. Building on this formulation, we introduce Verus-Insight, trained with human-anchored full-process supervision and progressive capability training to strengthen both fine-grained artifact detection and video-level detection. We further introduce Verus-Bench, a benchmark with fine-grained human annotations of perceptible artifacts for evaluating artifact detection. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that Verus-Insight achieves strong performance in both fine-grained artifact analysis and AI-generated video detection, with substantial gains in recovering human-perceived artifacts. Further analyses reveal that the three capabilities are complementary yet distinct, and that Verus-Insight more reliably converts relevant inspection targets into supported artifact evidence without increasing spurious artifact claims.
evidence_items.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Multimodal large-language-model (LLM) evidence pipelines often attach rule-derived outcomes to candidate remediation actions even though only the executed action yields a factual production outcome. Treating those counterfactual rules as ground truth can miscalibrate routing, while discarding them wastes structured operational knowledge. We introduce EviRoute-DR, a disagreement-reliability routing method that learns when rule priors fail and combines corrected-rule experts with direct factual outcome experts through a reliability-conditioned meta-learner. The study uses 2,100 production cases, seven candidate actions per case (14,700 case-action records), and exactly one observed production outcome per case. Base models are trained on 600 factual cases, combined on 200, and evaluated on 1,300 held-out factual cases spanning main, temporal-labelled, hard, and workflow-shift cohorts. On factual outcomes, EviRoute-DR achieves AUC 0.926 and Brier score 0.0910, compared with 0.921/0.0971 for direct logistic regression and 0.924/0.0922 for a random-forest baseline. The paired bootstrap Brier improvement over logistic regression is 0.0060 (95\% CI 0.0021--0.0092). A separate production-derived counterfactual replay shows a stronger cost-resolution frontier at moderate operating costs, reaching approximately 0.815 resolution near 12 cost units. Because the logged action is always the argmax of the production score vector, we do not interpret those scores as stochastic propensities and make no inverse-propensity, doubly robust causal, or production-effect claim. The results support disagreement-aware reliability fusion as a practical methodology for evidence routing under partial factual feedback.
evidence_items.title: Disagreement reliability routing for multimodal large language model evidence pipelines with imperfect counterfactual priors

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Objective This study aimed to compare the clinical quality of responses provided by four current large language models (LLMs) to orthopaedic patient questions based on expert evaluations and to investigate whether expert-rated response quality could be predicted using natural language processing (NLP), semantic representation, and machine learning methods. Materials and Methods Fifty patient-oriented questions covering anterior cruciate ligament injuries (n = 15), meniscal tears (n = 15), and total knee arthroplasty (n = 20) were submitted to ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, and Gemini, yielding 200 unique responses. All responses were independently evaluated by three orthopaedic specialists for Accuracy, Completeness, and Misinformation, generating 600 expert evaluations. Models were compared using paired statistical methods overall and at the clinical-category and question levels. NLP features were extracted from the responses, and semantic representations and question-response similarities were calculated using SBERT. An RBF-SVR model combining NLP, semantic, and explainable textual features was developed to predict response-level quality scores obtained by averaging the ratings of the three experts. To prevent data leakage, the four LLM responses to the same clinical question were kept within the same cross-validation fold, and final performance was evaluated using nested grouped cross-validation. Results The four LLMs achieved generally high Accuracy (3.607–3.827/4) and Completeness (3.633–3.780/4) scores and low Misinformation scores (0.093–0.127/2). Descriptively, Claude had the highest mean Accuracy (3.827 ± 0.288), whereas DeepSeek had the highest Completeness (3.780 ± 0.283) and the lowest Misinformation score (0.093 ± 0.243). However, no overall statistically significant differences were detected among the models for Accuracy (p = 0.070), Completeness (p = 0.361), or Misinformation (p = 0.451).
evidence_items.title: Predicting Expert-Rated Quality of Large Language Model Responses to Orthopaedic Patient Questions Using Computational Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background In Indonesia, people with communication disorders predominantly communicate using Bahasa Isyarat Indonesia (BISINDO). Nevertheless, all current systems for BISINDO recognition generate fragmented, word-by-word output and lack natural language generation (NLG) capabilities, thereby fundamentally constraining their communicative utility. Objective The aim of this study is to develop, validate, and field-evaluate SmartGlove BISINDO, an AI-assisted wearable sign language–to-speech system that embeds large language model (LLM)–powered NLG into a BISINDO translation pipeline for the first time. Methods This study followed the design science research (DSR) framework, covering phases 1 through 5 (problem identification, solution objectives, prototype design and development, demonstration, and evaluation). Data were collected from 12 purposively selected informants (6 domain experts and 6 deaf education companions/teachers) across 3 Indonesian cities (Malang, Surabaya, and Makassar), using a needs-analysis questionnaire and an expert validation sheet, and analyzed through statistical triangulation of agreement percentage, content validity ratio (CVR), and Aiken V. The validated prototype was field-tested in Makassar and Malang with 15 participants with communication disorders and 4 observers or companions; it was evaluated by a disability expert in Surabaya. Results The needs analysis yielded a grand mean of 4.77 (SD 0.51) across 4 clusters, with 89% mean agreement, indicating very high priority for all identified needs. The prototype’s 5-layer architecture integrates wearable sensors, on-device gesture classification, and LLM-based NLG. Expert validation showed an overall Aiken V of 0.94, with all 14 items exceeding the 0.75 validity cutoff and with 11/14 items (79%) rated highly valid (V>0.90).
evidence_items.title: The SmartGlove BISINDO Wearable Sensor and Large Language Model–Based Sign Language–to-Speech System for Users With Communication Disorders: Design Science Research Study

evidence_items.summary: Moral evaluation depends not only on what people do, but on why observers believe they acted as they did. Although motive inference has long been recognized as central to moral judgment, moral motivation itself has rarely been conceptualized as a multidimensional psychological representation. We investigated whether observers infer four distinct moral motivational dimensions (Approach Good, Avoid Bad, Approach Bad, and Avoid Good) from natural-language narratives and whether this representational structure is recovered by frontier large language models (LLMs). Human participants (N = 1,031) and 23 frontier LLMs evaluated 344 real-world moral narratives using identical procedures. All four motivational dimensions were inferred frequently in both populations and exhibited structured patterns of co-occurrence. Human observers clustered antisocial motivations (Approach Bad and Avoid Good) more strongly than prosocial motivations, whereas LLMs exhibited the opposite pattern. Across all evaluative outcomes, inferred motivations systematically predicted judgments of rightness, wrongness, praiseworthiness, and blameworthiness. Supervised machine learning analyses further demonstrated that the complete four-dimensional representation consistently outperformed every reduced two-dimensional alternative, indicating that each motivational dimension contributed unique predictive information. Although LLMs broadly recovered the multidimensional structure observed in humans, they inferred antisocial motivations less frequently, concentrated those attributions within fewer narratives, and produced systematically compressed response distributions characterized by lower variance and entropy. Together, these findings suggest that moral motivation is best understood as a multidimensional representational system and that representational richness provides a useful framework for evaluating both human moral cognition and its approximation by artificial systems.
evidence_items.title: Humans and Large Language Models Infer a Multidimensional Structure of Moral Motivation

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate and evaluate patient-facing medical materials. Through persona prompting, LLMs can be instructed to simulate responses from individuals with different demographic and experiential backgrounds, offering a scalable approach for approximating patient feedback. However, it remains unclear how closely these simulated persona-based responses reflect real patient perspectives, and whether this alignment is consistent across demographic subgroups. Objective This study assessed whether contemporary LLMs can simulate diverse patient perspectives on hospital discharge summaries when prompted with personas defined by education, gender, and health care use. We further examined whether persona-based simulation performance was equitable across subgroups by comparing LLM-generated responses with responses from a general-population human cohort under a standardized evaluation framework. Methods We evaluated 4 contemporary LLMs, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Opus 4.6, against responses from 99 participants recruited through Prolific (Prolific Academic Ltd). Participants answered 10 questions for discharge summaries that varied in length and medical complexity. Questions included information-based items assessing factual comprehension and perception-based items assessing subjective understanding. Model-human alignment was measured using modal mean absolute error and expected absolute ordinal distance. We also conducted a chain-of-thought sensitivity analysis for cases with the greatest divergence between LLM-generated persona and matched human responses. Results Across LLMs, persona responses aligned more closely with human responses on information-based items than on perception-based items.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Models’ Simulation of Patient Comprehension of Discharge Summaries: Multimodel Evaluation Study

evidence_items.summary: Importance: Patients increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) for health-related conversations, but evaluation measures largely reflect clinician judgment. Objective: To develop and preliminarily evaluate a patient instrument assessing the quality of patient-AI health conversations. Design: Cross-sectional survey conducted June 5-14, 2026, following patient-partnered instrument development and cognitive interviews. Setting: An anonymous online survey. Participants: A convenience sample of adults with prior use of large language models for personal health-related queries, recruited from an academic medical center-affiliated Insight Panel and patient peers. Exposures: Participants' own prior health-related conversations with AI tools of their choosing. Main Outcomes and Measures: The Patient-AI Rating instrument comprised 12 communication-quality and patient engagement items rated from 1 to 5 and a separately scored patient-perceived-harm item. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach alpha, with sensitivity analyses using first ratings only for those using the tool to rate multiple conversations and participant-mean profiles. We examined item-total correlations, inter-item structure, and between- and within-participant variation. Results: Fourteen participants contributed 46 complete ratings; among 13 providing demographics, median age was 63 years (IQR, 53-70 years), and 8 (62%) reported female gender. Participants provided a median of 2 ratings (range, 1-17). Cronbach alpha was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.93) across all ratings, 0.85 using first ratings only, and 0.92 using participant-mean profiles. Corrected item-total correlations ranged from 0.42 to 0.72; mean inter-item correlation was 0.40. No item deletion improved Cronbach alpha. The mean quality score was 4.43 (SD, 0.45). Among 9 participants contributing multiple ratings, the intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.45, suggesting inter-conversation variability.
evidence_items.title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of the Patient-Artificial Intelligence Rating Instrument

evidence_items.summary: The rapid ubiquity of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally disrupted traditional pedagogical frameworks in engineering education, necessitating a critical examination of its impact on cognitive development and knowledge retention. This longitudinal study spans 30 years (1996–2025) to analyse shifts in student learning curves within an AI curriculum, testing the hypothesis that reliance on automated tools exacerbates a ‘J-curve’ learning style, characterised by delayed engagement and terminal production spikes, at the expense of fundamental understanding. By comparing weekly topic acquisition and final assessment data across cohorts, the research reveals a distinct morphological transformation from the classic sigmoidal progression (‘S-curve’) of the baseline 1996 class to an exponential ‘J-curve’ in the 2025 cohort. While modern students demonstrate high procedural efficiency in project delivery, this shift correlates strongly with a significant decline in independent examination performance, where mean scores fell from 9.50 to 7.75. Although a gradual decline in performance was observed prior to 2020, the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent ubiquity of generative AI tools may have intensified this trend (main finding). The data indicate that students utilise AI to bypass the cognitive friction necessary for deep learning, resulting in a failure to exit the assisted phase of skill acquisition. These findings suggest that current AI integration acts as a mechanism for cognitive offloading rather than scaffolding, creating a trade-off between immediate output and long-term declarative competence. The study concludes that engineering curricula must rigorously re-evaluate assessment strategies to ensure that the efficiency of automated generation does not erode the foundational logic required for sustainable innovation.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Learning Flow in 30 Years

organizations: Department of Mathematics and computational science  SRI KRISHNA KNOWLEDGE FOUNDATION  Deemed to be University
evidence_items.summary: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has become an important research direction because intelligent systems are increasingly used to support decisions in complex and uncertain environments. However, the interpretability of a decision depends not only on the final prediction but also on the mathematical structure through which the prediction is obtained. This paper develops an algebraic framework for interpretable multi-criteria decision-making based on bounded ordered structures, weighted aggregation, and explicit criterion-level contributions. A finite set of alternatives is evaluated using normalized criteria, and a weighted score is assigned to each alternative. The framework represents criterion values in a bounded lattice and uses an order-preserving aggregation operator to obtain transparent rankings. Mathematical properties concerning monotonicity, boundedness, score decomposition, and stability under perturbations are established. An illustrative numerical example involving the selection of an artificial intelligence model demonstrates how the framework generates rankings and human-readable explanations. The approach provides a mathematically explicit foundation for decision support and can be extended to fuzzy, linguistic, and neutrosophic environments. The proposed framework and numerical example are illustrative; novelty and performance claims require literature verification and empirical validation. Keywords: Abstract algebra; lattice theory; explainable artificial intelligence; multi-criteria decision-making; interpretable decision systems; weighted aggregation.
evidence_items.title: Algebraic Structures for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Decision-Making Systems

evidence_items.summary: Background. Knowledge-graph models can rank existing drugs for a disease, but their benchmarks mostly reward rediscovering known treatments, and their scores rarely come with evidence a researcher can check. We built OREVID, an open tool that shows a ranked candidate only when an evidence line supports it and reports how often each line was right on held-out data, and compared it with TxGNN on identical data. Methods. The graph combines PrimeKG, Open Targets, STRING and PubTator3 (157,822 nodes, 9.46 million edges). For each disease, 22 degree-weighted metapath features feed a LightGBM LambdaRank model trained with masked neighbourhoods. A candidate is shown only if it is indicated for an ontology-neighbour disease or for a disease sharing at least 3 associated genes (hypergeometric p &lt; 10⁻⁵ over the genes with at least one associated disease). The acceptance criteria for these rules were set in advance; the rules were revised on the hidden-treatment benchmarks and then measured on an external set of approvals not used to choose them. TxGNN was retrained with its official code on the same PrimeKG splits, and all tasks and predictions are released as OREVID-bench. Results. Zero-shot Recall@100 (mean ± SD over five splits) was 0.811 ± 0.042 for OREVID, 0.412 ± 0.042 for TxGNN and 0.358 ± 0.040 for a popularity baseline, with OREVID ahead on every split (paired difference with TxGNN 0.399, 95% CI 0.352–0.443, resampling diseases). On nine disease areas held out it was 0.617 against 0.237, ahead in all nine, although TxGNN had the higher AUPRC in five. Training OREVID without validation labels and excluding diseases where TxGNN outputs constant scores gave 0.809 against 0.421.
evidence_items.title: OREVID: Open, Evidence-Based Drug Repurposing with a Benchmark Against TxGNN

evidence_items.summary: We present a computational benchmark for large Dirichlet eigenvalue spectra on triaxial ellipsoids, comparing finite-element discretizations combined with ARPACK, inertia-based spectrum slicing (SLEPc/MUMPS), a stretched spectral Galerkin (SSG) method, and a multi-probe block-Hankel filter diagonalization that we extend here from a landmark detector into a gap-free complete-spectrum solver. Rather than ranking methods by runtime alone, we ask whether the resulting spectra preserve reliable geometric information. The unit ball serves as a quality-assurance case, since its eigenvalues are known in closed form; for the triaxial case a=1, b=1.5, c=2.3 we add a reverse-geometry validation based on the three-term Weyl law, reconstructing volume, surface area, and integrated mean curvature from finite spectral segments. As the eigenvalue index grows, the error is increasingly dominated by the mesh rather than by the eigensolver. SSG gives the strongest geometric consistency in our tests, reconstructing the volume to about 0.025%. The block-Hankel method extended by a Weyl-equal-count tiling, an analytic one-sided bandpass, and coprime decimation voting produces a complete ordered spectrum of 2034 levels including multiplicities; spectrum slicing returns the same 2034 levels on the identical matrices in 4.9 core-hours against roughly 69,400. For this task, the established method is therefore superior by four orders of magnitude, and we report that plainly. What the comparison establishes instead is agreement; three unrelated solvers on one discretization coincide to a median relative deviation of 3×10−11, with Sylvester inertia counts certifying the level count exactly. On the unit ball, where degeneracies reach 2ℓ+1=51, the certified spectrum reproduces the exact level count without deviation up to λ=600 and resolves degeneracies up to 35.
evidence_items.title: Hearing Ellipsoids: A Benchmark of Krylov, Spectral Galerkin, and Filter Diagonalization Eigensolvers

evidence_items.summary: We introduce a core–virtual-complete variant of mixed-reference spin-flip time-dependent density functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT), CV-MRSF, which completes the block of core-to-virtual (CV) excitations. For each CV excitation, the four determinants missing from MRSF-TDDFT are recovered by imposing exact spin adaptation, which makes every singlet and triplet spin pure and gives the proper singlet–triplet splitting of CV states without spin-pairing couplings. In addition, invariance under a rotation of the two singly occupied molecular orbitals (SOMOs) O1 and O2 adds the configurations C¹O₁²V¹ and C¹O₂²V¹. The number of CV configurations per excitation thus grows from one to four in the singlet and to five in the triplet configuration state function (CSF) response, and one quintet CSF also arises within the same CV block, instead of from a separate spin-flip-up calculation. As a result, the CV excitations properly couple to the complete set of open-to-open (OO) configurations, both singlet and triplet, as well as to the core-to-open (CO) and open-to-virtual (OV) configurations, which relaxes the excited states and accounts for most of the changes in excitation energy. For hybrid functionals, a spin-scalar one-body correction keeps the response matrix covariant under separate rotations of the core, open-shell, and virtual orbitals. For the Thiel benchmark set it lowers the mean absolute error of MRSF-TDDFT from 0.53 to 0.40 eV for the singlets and from 0.40 to 0.29 eV for the triplets. The largest gains are for n→π states by excitation character and nucleobase singlets by molecule class. The CV block also describes the spin-pure triplet-pair states ¹(TT), ³(TT), and ⁵(TT) of chromophore dimers on the same footing, the essential requirement for the description of singlet fission processes.
evidence_items.title: Eliminating the remaining spin contamination of MRSF-TDDFT by completing its core–virtual block

evidence_items.summary: This study examines a fully implicit finite difference scheme based on extended cubic B-spline collocation for solving one-dimensional tim236e-fractional advection–diffusion equations. The time-fractional derivative is approximated using the Caputo formulation with the L1 discretization scheme, while the spatial derivatives are approximated using extended cubic B-spline basis functions. The resulting fully discrete system incorporates the memory effects of the fractional derivative together with the prescribed initial and boundary conditions. The stability and convergence properties of the scheme are examined through Fourier analysis and mathematical approximation estimates under appropriate assumptions. The numerical performance is assessed using two benchmark problems with known analytical solutions. Comparisons of the published numerical and exact solutions demonstrate good agreement, while the reported error norms and spatial refinement results indicate decreasing numerical errors as the spatial grid is refined. The findings support the accuracy and applicability of the fully implicit extended cubic B-spline collocation scheme for the considered benchmark problems.
evidence_items.title: Stability and Benchmark-Based Convergence Assessment of Extended Cubic B-Spline Collocation for Time-Fractional Advection-Diffusion Equations

evidence_items.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping cybersecurity, moving it from signature-based reactive security to agentic, self-evolving, and proactive operations. However, the fast deployment of autonomous agents entails significant security issues, physical-layer attacks in cyber-physical systems, alignment problems, and advanced social engineering risks jeopardizing the stability of the modern sociotechnical infrastructures. This survey paper, which summarizes and analyses the literature, examines the duality of AI in cybersecurity, exploring its implications for strengthening digital defences and increasing the threat landscape for adversaries. We perform a thorough review of 36 cutting-edge research articles, which are organized into six important areas: self-evolving defensive paradigms, LLM-based intelligent agents, reinforcement learning for autonomous decision-making, security of cyber-physical systems, human-machine co-teaming, and agent alignment. Our synthesis shows that multi-agent collaborations greatly shorten incident response times and automate discovery of vulnerabilities but are also highly vulnerable to prompt injection, training data poisoning, and physical-layer spoofing. Moreover, we identify a shift from model patches to model alignment and constitutional safety at runtime as a prerequisite for securing these systems. We believe that resilient digital defence must also be considered a sociotechnical problem, as there must be agents, autonomous systems, that are governed by other agents, aligned and constitutionally bound, and are able to collaborate, rather than operate completely separately, with human operators.
evidence_items.title: Cyber Defence, Agentic AI, and the Sociotechnical Paradigm: A Survey of AI-Driven Cybersecurity

evidence_items.summary: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models. On block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin. For visual token merging, it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.
evidence_items.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

evidence_items.summary: Human motion, environmental contacts, and interaction forces are governed by common physical laws, yet existing approaches typically separate visual pose reconstruction from contact and force estimation. This separation limits joint reasoning and can propagate errors between stages. We introduce PACT, an end-to-end model that jointly learns to estimate human pose, contacts and contact forces from monocular video. Our approach augments a human reconstruction foundation model with learnable contact-force tokens and a temporal transformer that integrates visual features with world-space motion. Joint prediction heads refine human poses and estimate contacts and forces, while physics-based supervision encourages consistency between the reconstructed motion and interaction forces. To address the scarcity of force annotations, we develop a data annotation pipeline that combines contact labeling with physics-based motion and force optimization, producing training supervision from synthetic and real-world videos. We also introduce a real-world climbing benchmark ForceWall with climbing videos and corresponding ground-truth contact forces obtained from the force sensors. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art contact and force estimation, outperforming staged reconstruction approaches and generalizing to interactions beyond the training distribution. These results support end-to-end joint learning as an effective approach to recovering human motion and physical interactions from video.
evidence_items.title: PACT: End-to-End Learning of Human Pose, Contacts, and Forces from Video

evidence_items.summary:
Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone. Recent work recovers the hidden reasoning by replaying encrypted blocks across models. It somehow works, but it breaks the providers' terms of service, so it is not something a product can be built on long-term.
  We built the alternative. We take the context and the teacher's answer as input, and generate the reasoning trace ourselves, in the style of the student's own model family. Training is two-stage, supervised and then adversarial: a generator learns to regenerate the family's own reasoning traces from their context and answer, and a critic learns how real a reasoning trace looks. Applied to a teacher's answer, the generator writes one in the family's style. An independent judge rates how likely traces are to be genuine on a scale from 0 to 1: ours average 0.68, real traces 0.66, and traces selected by the critic from four candidates 0.82. These are authenticity scores, not correctness rates.
  We test the idea on five benchmarks with everything else held fixed. On general tasks the five training corpora are about the same; on coding, the generated reasoning beats Fable 5's own thinking content. With the same 5,000 questions and the same teacher answers, HumanEval+ improves by 3.7 points and MBPP+ by 7.1 at the final checkpoint, and the MBPP+ lead holds at every checkpoint. We suspect that reasoning written in the student's family style is easier for it to learn from.
evidence_items.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking

evidence_items.summary: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves data efficiency but generalizes worse to distant worlds under single-world training; (2) we observe an early interface phase with broad cross-world benefits and a later world phase with gains narrowed to in-corpus and related worlds, and fit an empirical scaling law relating validation loss to data volume, diversity and model size; and (3) our models are competitive with Minecraft specialists and frontier models in 3D worlds, and perform best in real-time settings. However, the limits of imitation and persistent gaps in distant worlds suggest that building generalist embodied agents requires richer training stages beyond continued pre-training.
evidence_items.title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds

evidence_items.summary: Aiming to modify textual content while preserving the original style, Scene Text Editing (STE) has significant practical value in many applications. STE typically requires paired images before and after editing for training. However, recent approaches rely heavily on synthetic paired data and complex disentanglement strategies. They struggle to faithfully capture the diversity and complexity of natural scenes, often producing artifacts or hallucinations. In this work, we challenge the common practice and investigate whether STE can be driven by turning each real sample into its own paired supervision. Concretely, we explore multiple ways to disrupt the original image (e.g., Crop, Shuffle, Mask) to construct self-paired training data, and build a strong baseline (TextRIRO}) upon a conditional diffusion architecture. Our experiments show that combining character-column shuffling with image cropping (Shuffle&Crop) effectively destroys text semantics while preserving key style cues, enabling the model to learn editing behaviors directly from the real text image. With this concise yet real-oriented design, TextRIRO achieves promising performance in both accuracy and visual realism across real-world benchmarks, substantially mitigating the synthetic-to-real domain gap. Furthermore, we leverage TextRIRO to build TextRIRO-3M, a large-scale realistic dataset for long-text recognition by concatenating edited and original images. Experimental results show that training recognition models with TextRIRO-3M significantly improves recognition accuracy, demonstrating that TextRIRO provides highly useful training resources for downstream tasks. Overall, TextRIRO lifts STE to realistic, reliable, and widely applicable new levels. Code is available at https://github.com/YesianRohn/TextRIRO.
evidence_items.title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?

evidence_items.summary: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. We introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination, instantiated through ten task-specific metrics on a 0-100 scale. Evaluating 37 distinct models across 300 test cases, we find that high visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency. In particular, request execution remains challenging: the highest task-specific scores are 36.90 for Following among seven avatar-performance models, 25.93 for Following in text-conditioned world generation, and 15.00 for Edit Success among three reported reference-editing models. These findings identify reliable request execution under timing and preservation constraints as a central challenge for advancing omni-modal real-time interactive systems. The leaderboard is available at https://streameval.ai
evidence_items.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models

It analyses the transition from the EU GDPR to the UK GDPR, incorporates the implications of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, and evaluates recent case law and regulatory guidance relevant to contemporary data protection practice. The book explains key areas of compliance, including data security, breach notification duties, international data transfers, electronic communications, and the responsibilities of Data Protection Officer and other privacy professionals. It also addresses the practical challenges that organizations, legal practitioners, and compliance specialists encounter when implementing effective data governance within rapidly evolving technological and regulatory environments.
